baseline.stable_ids: F01 through F84 are retained by the checker; append new independently corrected defects.

evidence_policy: Coverage means a concrete valid automated check has been registered for a distinct historical defect. Mechanical validation cannot establish assertion quality or historical reproduction; consult docs/regression-audit.md and owning CI jobs. Other-platform and release-only checks are not claimed to execute on the current host.

defects.description: Parallel clipboard regression fixtures reused temporary files, producing cross-test clipboard results
defects.notes: Hosted macOS CI reproduced the wrong-fixture result. Atomic allocation and exclusive directory creation isolate each fixture; the concurrent test preserves this contract.

defects.description: Mobile FFI constructor discarded initialization errors and returned a usable client after configuration failure
defects.notes: The isolated bad-config child fails against the ignored-error constructor and passes with propagation. F53 fixed App.init itself; this distinct public FFI caller still discarded the returned error.

defects.description: Release publication exposed a public release before completing and verifying its uploaded asset set
defects.notes: The actual publication shell runs against an isolated GitHub fixture. A changed uploaded evidence file must leave the release unpublished; a valid complete set is verified before the public transition. Windows skips the Ubuntu publication-shell fixture rather than claiming local execution.

defects.description: Revocation removed a device routing entry before sending Close, leaving its authenticated socket open; rejected member handshakes could also register before validation
defects.notes: The old source times out waiting for Close. The fixed handler captures the sender before removing routing state and validates member authorization before registration. Actual websocket regression checks Close, post-close send rejection, preserved owner Ping, revoked state/epoch and rejected reconnect. RED/GREEN was observed on macOS; each platform registration still requires its CI execution.

defects.description: Relay credential loading blocked indefinitely opening a FIFO before rejecting non-regular files
defects.notes: One file-opening defect across three configuration paths, not three defects. With production source 822af5d1 and the new bounded tests, all three writer-less 0600 FIFO cases hit the five-second child-process rejection deadline. Unix nonblocking open followed by descriptor metadata validation passes them while preserving certificate/key symlinks. Local RED/GREEN was recorded on macOS; Linux requires its owning CI execution and Windows does not use these Unix FIFO fixtures.

defects.description: Release publication rejected valid Windows GNU binary-mode checksum records by comparing their formatting with Linux text-mode output
defects.notes: The 8ee9fbf publication shell replayed with the Windows hash-space-asterisk-basename fixture fails before release mutation; the fixed publisher accepts that exact record format. The helper also verifies the actual archive digest and exact basename, rather than accepting arbitrary checksum-file outputs. Windows names the artifact format; these Python/publication fixtures execute in the Unix CI jobs, not on a claimed Windows host.

defects.description: A container run waiting for a release could publish its old source revision after the release tag had been retargeted
defects.notes: Actual local Git repositories retain an old workflow SHA on the default branch while the remote tag is moved to another commit. The prior ancestry-only guard still accepts it; the fixed fresh-fetch tag comparison rejects it. The same source check runs before candidate package writes and again after provenance verification before final version promotion. Deleted tags and changed default branches are related source-binding variants, not extra defects. The fixture writes only disposable local repositories and calls no remote hosting service.

defects.description: A failed reconstruction rerun overwrote the report source identity while leaving an earlier run's success markers in the same report directory
defects.notes: Replaying the wrapper before c847d2d in its synthetic Docker fixture with a pre-existing success report and failing first build changes source-commit.txt but retains old comparison.txt/reproduced.sha256. The corrected wrapper creates a source-bound report child for every invocation and emits success markers only after both builds and comparisons succeed. Integrated as c5ad280. This is report-lifecycle regression evidence, not an actual independent-build result.

defects.description: The reconstruction recipe left its Docker architecture selected by the host and did not bind a recorded target platform to both builds and runs
defects.notes: The pre-c847d2d wrapper passes no Docker --platform argument and records no platform, so its multiarch base recipe does not identify one stable cross-host reconstruction target. The Docker fixture now verifies linux/amd64 by default and an explicit linux/arm64 choice for both independent builds and runs, with platform.txt retained. This environment-identity failure is distinct from F92 report reuse. These argument/recording fixtures do not prove actual cross-architecture output identity. Integrated as c5ad280.

defects.description: The mobile integration fixture treated the room-file write as completion before background pairing had persisted its sync configuration
defects.notes: This intermittent test-readiness race was observed during the workspace suite; the fixture now waits for the persisted sync-enabled boundary before checking daemon behavior. It is a fixture correction, not a newly claimed mobile product defect. The targeted current test passes, but the old fixture can also pass intermittently and no deterministic focused regression has been established. Nearby passing coverage receives no credit.
